the mean lifetimes for three of the lowest transitions in the SD band of133Nd have been determined.

the superdeformed states have lifetimes that are longer than predicted by theoretical calculations and the reduced transition probability of the K-forbidden 21/2→17/2 transition is hindered by a factor of ~10.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the band is not K-forbidden, and the bandhead of the band has an intrinsic quadrupole moment of about 5 eb.
the superdeformed states are well described by the Nilsson-Strutinsky model, and the hindrance of the transitions that feed the band are consistent with K-forbiddenness.
the superdeformed states are well deformed and have lifetimes consistent with the expected K-forbiddenness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the superdeformed bands in133Nd are consistent with a rotational model, and that the band is not hindered by K-forbiddenness.
the superdeformed states in133Nd have a mean lifetime of 0.5±0.2 ns and a quadrupole moment of 7.5±1.0 eb.
the superdeformed bands of133Nd and135La are similar in that the low spin members of both bands are consistent with the predictions of the cranked shell model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the K-forbiddenness of the 25+/2→17+ and 25+/2 →21+/2 transitions is not large.
there is a significant hindrance of the 21+/2→19/2 and 23+/2→19+/2 transitions in the band.
the superdeformed states in133Nd are not hindered as much as those in the other superdeformed nuclei, and the hindrance is consistent with a 1p-0h transition.
